issues.description: Pacing comment promises 'real-time pacing' but code only chunks bytes — no timing.
issues.detail: The changelog and inline comment claim 'real-time pacing' via fixed_audio_packet_size, but the implementation just slices the buffer and sends as fast as the caller writes. There is no sleep, no _next_send_time interaction, no _send_interval gate. Either wire pacing through or stop calling it pacing. Words should match the diff.

issues.description: Renaming a public param without a deprecation alias breaks every existing caller silently.
issues.detail: The changed.md says 'Renamed audio_packet_bytes to fixed_audio_packet_size.' Pydantic will silently ignore the old kwarg (extra='ignore' is the default on TransportParams in most setups) and the user gets unpacketized audio with no error. Either keep a deprecated alias with a warning, or be explicit it is a breaking change in the changelog.

issues.description: fixed_audio_packet_size has no validation — zero, negative, or odd values misbehave.
issues.detail: A value of 0 falls through the truthy check fine, but a negative or non-multiple-of-sample-width int will silently produce garbage PCM (split a 16-bit sample mid-byte) or infinite empty chunks. Validate >0 and a multiple of frame size at param construction, or document the constraint loudly. Right now it is a foot-gun.

issues.description: Non-audio payloads bypass the buffer but buffered audio ahead of them is not flushed.
issues.detail: If JSON control payloads are interleaved with PCM, the buffered remainder PCM stays parked while the JSON ships immediately. Order is reversed on the wire. Either flush partial audio (zero-padded) before the control message, or document that control frames jump the queue. Caller will not expect this.

issues.description: Vonage DTMF dual-format lookup is speculative cleverness, not protocol.
issues.detail: `digit = message.get('digit') or message.get('dtmf', {}).get('digit')` covers two shapes 'just in case.' Pick the documented one. If the spec really sends both, comment which Vonage version emits which. Right now it reads like the author was not sure, which is exactly the kind of code a maintainer six years from now will curse.

issues.description: Serializer has no tests in the diff.
issues.detail: New protocol serializer, new transport branch, zero unit tests in this PR. Round-trip serialize/deserialize, the packetization buffer with a remainder, the InterruptionFrame clear path — all easy to cover and all the kind of thing that silently rots. 'Patches-and-the-tests-better-pass' applies.

review.summary: Patch is roughly the right shape — a serializer plus a small transport hook — and the diff is readable. But the marketing ('real-time pacing') overshoots what the code does: it is chunking, not pacing. The rename of audio_packet_bytes is a silent breaking change with no alias. The packet-size knob is unvalidated and will quietly produce broken audio on bad input. No tests landed with a new wire protocol. NEEDS-WORK: clarify or implement the pacing claim, add a deprecation alias, validate the packet size, and ship at least minimal unit tests before this lands.
